question:
A 28-year-old man presents with sharp neck pain that began upon waking this morning. He reports
difficulty turning his head to the left but denies any injury, though he suspects he may have slept in an
awkward position on the couch. Acetaminophen and a warm compress provided no relief, prompting
him to seek medical care. He has no prior history of similar symptoms, denies pain radiation, and has
no other complaints. His medical history is unremarkable, and he does not take any medications
regularly. On structural examination, tenderness and hypertonicity are noted in the cervical
paravertebral muscles and scalenes. The vertebrae from C4 to C6 resist right translation, and during
neck flexion from a neutral position, C5 rotates further to the right. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Answer Choices: (A) C4–C5 ERLSR (B) C4–C6 FRRSR (C) C4–C6 NSRRR (D) C5–C6 ERRSR (E)
C4–C6 NSRRL with somatic dysfunction (F) C4–C6 ERRSR with compensatory rotation (G) C4–C6
ERRSR (H) C4–C6 FSRRR (I) C5–C6 FSRRL (J) C4–C6 NSRRL
 A. C4–C5 ERLSR
B. C4–C6 FRRSR
C. C5–C6 FSRRL
D. C4–C6 ERRSR
E. C4–C6 FSRRR
F. C4–C6 NSRRL with somatic dysfunction
G. C4–C6 NSRRR
